newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures mostly lower at close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures mostly lower at close.

text.p: Most NYMEX electricity futures closed lower amid weather forecasts calling for mild conditions in the western U.S., market sources said.
"It was a pretty lackluster market. We will probably see more consolidation this week," said one trader.
Sources also cited a growing regional supply of power as helping to put a damper on both cash electricity and futures prices.
Over the weekend, two 550 megawatt (MW) coal-fired units in Wyoming, one at the Jim Bridger plant and one at Laramie River Station, were restarted after maintenance outages.

In addition, a 1,221 MW unit at the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona and a 1,087 MW unit at the Diablo Canyon nuclear plant in central California recently resumed full power after refueling outages.
But another 1,221 MW unit at Palo Verde was cut back to 60 percent power for unplanned repairs, which are expected to finish early Tuesday.
Forecasts called for below-normal temperatures in the Southwest through the end of the week, with near normal temperatures seen in the six to 10-day outlook.
The Pacific Northwest was expected to see temperatures near to slightly above-normal through the next 10 days or so.
The July Palo Verde (PV) contract fell 29 cents to close at $27.63 per megawatt hour (MWh), after trading as high as $28.00.
August PV fell 31 cents to close at $30.80, its low for the day. September PV lost 15 cents to settle at $27.32.
July California Oregon Border (COB) fell 21 cents to close at $17.21 per MWh, compared with a high for the day of $17.50 and a low of $17.10.
August COB fell 37 cents to settle at $21.70, while September fell 15 cents to $21.95.
Other electricity contracts ended flat to mixed.
NYMEX said as of 1535 EDT an estimated total of 740 COB and 240 PV contracts had traded.
